findings.title: A global group view grant is treated as permission to manage groups
findings.body: `canManage()` evaluates both `view` and `manage` on the all-groups resource. Consequently, a principal granted only the `view` scope passes `requireManage()` for operations that do not yet have a concrete group, including `POST /groups`. That permits creating top-level groups and moving an existing group to the top level, despite the policy granting read-only access. Only the `manage` scope should satisfy this method.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions realms are never initialized with the new Groups schema
findings.body: `init()` returns as soon as an admin-permissions client already exists. Realms created with the previous V2 schema therefore retain no `Groups` resource, no group scopes, and no group-specific resources after an upgrade. Creating a group scope permission then fails because `getScope()` cannot find the new scope, while group evaluators cannot resolve the all-groups resource. Initialization needs to reconcile missing schema scopes/resources for an existing admin-permissions client, or an explicit migration is required.

findings.title: Resources created for individual groups are not assigned the Groups type
findings.body: When `getOrCreateResource()` creates a resource for a group ID, it updates its scopes but never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)`. `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` discovers scoped group grants using `findByType(..., "Groups", ...)`, so these individual resources are not discovered at all. As a result, group-member grants are omitted from the group filter used by user search/count operations; authorized users can disappear from paged searches and counts. Newly created resources need their schema resource type assigned.

findings.title: Group-member discovery uses authorization resource IDs as realm group IDs
findings.body: The callback receives an authorization `Resource`, but passes `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission()` and adds that same value to the returned set. Authorization resource IDs are generated independently from the realm group ID; the domain group ID is the resource name established by `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup()`. This makes the name lookup in `hasPermission()` miss the individual resource and sends opaque authorization IDs as `UserModel.GROUPS` to the user provider. Scoped group-member grants therefore do not filter users correctly, and an all-groups member grant can filter every user out. Use the resource name/domain group ID for both operations.

findings.title: Listing groups re-evaluates a global authorization policy for every group
findings.body: The previous `canViewGlobal` short circuit was removed, so every group in a non-hierarchical listing now calls `groupsEvaluator.canView(group)`. Under V2, even an all-groups `view` grant causes each call to look up/evaluate the authorization resource and its policies before falling back to the all-groups resource. This changes a global-view list from one policy evaluation to one evaluation per returned group (and the same regression exists in `GroupResource.getSubGroups`), which is expensive for realms with many groups. Cache `groupsEvaluator.canView()` once and only evaluate individual groups when it is false.
